To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the presence of rhetorical features in proverbs enhances perceptual fluency and decreases conceptual fluency; (b) the combination of rhetorical features facilitates choices for persuasive purposes; and (c) the effects of rhetorical brevitas are modulated by its interaction with other rhetorical features.
rhyme, meter, brevitas, and their combination enhance prosodic fluency, decrease conceptual fluency, and predict choices for persuasive purposes.
rhyme, meter, brevitas, and their combination facilitate perceptual fluency while handicapping ease in semantic comprehension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel framework for rhetorical features that integrates the effects of rhetorical devices into a more comprehensive model of language processing.
the interplay of prosodic and semantic fluency and with the effects of rhetorical devices on the fluency of language processing.
the interplay between rhetorical features of language and their effects on processing fluency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
rhetorical features may enhance or impair ease of processing, depending on the dimension of processing, type of fluency, and presence of other rhetorical features.
the effects of a single rhetorical feature on ease of processing depend on the specific dimension of processing, the type of fluency, and the presence or absence of other rhetorical features.
the presence of rhetorical features of language may enhance perceptual fluency while decreasing conceptual fluency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of rhetorical language are not uniform but rather depend on the type of processing and the type of fluency.
the effects of rhetorical language features are highly sensitive to the specific combination of features and that the effects of a combination may differ from those of the individual components.
the presence of a combination of rhetorical features facilitates perceptual (proposodic) fluency and enhances choices for persuasion, but it handicaps ease of conceptual (semantic) comprehension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rhetorical features may be used in a complementary fashion to achieve the most effective persuasive communication.
the effects of rhetorical devices may be predicted based on the specific type of fluency and rhetorical features involved.
the same rhetorical features can have opposite effects on different dimensions of processing ease.
